body: The flat pixel buffer GuiOS draws every frame through. It had no test for as long as it lived in `apps/guios/GuiDisplay.codex`; moving it into the foreword is the moment to give it one, because a chapter any application can now reach is a chapter whose clipping had better hold.

author: reek
body: Measured 2026-07-28 against seed B9875136: every reading below is CORRECT, and the chapter is pinned rather than repaired. Two sabotages fired, each on exactly its own row:

author: reek
body: Four writes outside the buffer and one inside. The inside one is the control: a clip that rejected everything would leave an empty grid and look exactly like a clip that works.

author: reek
body: Reading outside answers 0 rather than a neighbouring row, which is what an unclipped read would do: index -1 in a flat buffer is the pixel above and to the left, not nothing.

author: reek
body: A rect must fill exactly its own area. Asking for one that starts at (2,1) and is 3 by 2 leaves the row above, the column to the left and the bottom row untouched, and a rect off by one in either axis moves a character in this grid.

author: reek
body: A horizontal line clamps both ends instead of wrapping into the next row. Asked for -2 to 99 on row 2 it fills that row and nothing else.

author: reek
body: A vertical line skips the rows above the buffer and still draws the part inside it, which is a different behaviour from refusing the whole line.

author: reek
body: Four edges and a hollow middle. A 6 by 4 outline at (1,0) must leave the interior at (2,1) and (3,1) untouched; a version that filled would show no gap.
